mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where housing starts declined for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenues and profits grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the periods where real personal consumption expenditures increased over the last three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a tight labor market with strong job growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the unemployment rate was below 4% and nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate was above 4% and the Consumer Price Index increased by more than 0.3% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDP declined by more than 0.5% in the last quarter.
